summary: Inspected and downloaded the latest successful NOEMA Discovery artifact (115 Crossref candidates; priority 30: 4 RECENT_PUBLICATION, 2 UPCOMING_OR_AHEAD_OF_PRINT, 24 NEWLY_INDEXED_LEGACY). The first same-day pass staged 8 candidates. A later same-day scan found 2 additional non-duplicate candidates: the peer-reviewed PNAS Second Plague phylochronology paper (DOI 10.1073/pnas.2534899123) and the peer-reviewed J-STAGE computational language-acquisition study (DOI 10.5715/jnlp.33.1116). The daily pack now references 10 candidates cumulatively. No candidate was promoted to evidence, no historical relationship was generated, and model-generated behavior was explicitly kept non-evidentiary.
research_note: Highest-priority supplemental review: SECOND_PLAGUE_PHYLOCHRONOLOGY, because Phylogenetically Informed Radiocarbon Modeling narrows dating intervals and tentatively maps 75 Yersinia pestis genomes to documented outbreaks, but modeled/documentary association is not direct event identity. LANGUAGE_ACQUISITION_MODEL_VALIDITY is medium priority: child-like U-shaped curves in small language models are computational comparisons, not evidence of human cognitive mechanism. Existing review pressure from millet chronology, Wuwangdun continuity, Oaxaca figure correction, Hadrian lightning ritual, Kartal full-text access, Miyake dating, modern altered-state transfer and legacy burial/ancestor-worship literature remains open.
